We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied first two templates, got intermediate products. Need to continue applying remaining templates sequentially to generate a route tree.

We need to construct JSON route: root molecule is target SMILES O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O.

First reaction uses template 29646, producing some precursors (list). The apply_template returned three possible outcomes (tuples). Need to pick one that can be further processed with next template 1914389. We already applied 1914389 to one of those outcomes: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". That seems to be one of the products from first template. So route: target -> reaction 29646 -> precursor A (the one we used). Then reaction 1914389 on that precursor yields two products (tuple). The result: (('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'),). So two precursors: product1 and product2.

Now need to apply template 1914390 to one of these? The order must be as given, so after 1914389 we apply 1914390 to each appropriate precursor? Typically each reaction splits a molecule into precursors; we need a linear route of 5 steps, each step applying next template to one of the precursors (maybe the main fragment). We'll assume we continue on the main carbon skeleton (first precursor) and treat the second as a side product (maybe a reagent). For simplicity, we can include both as children of reaction node.

Thus reaction 1914390 applied to first precursor "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". Let's check matching.
